workflow_norms.norm: CLAUDE.md governance: concise, checked into git, describes Bash commands / code style / workflow rules. Run /init to generate a starter then refine. Remove any line that wouldn't cause mistakes if deleted.

Context compaction: intervene at ~60% context utilization (auto-compact triggers at ~80-90%). Use /compact with specific instructions ('Focus on the API changes'). Session Memory now writes summaries continuously so /compact is near-instant.

TDD as AI governance: use red/green/refactor as a built-in success condition that both developer and agent can verify. Prevents blind adoption of AI output. Be explicit with Claude that you are doing TDD to prevent premature mock implementations.

Multi-agent pattern: decompose tasks then summon subagents to work autonomously. Agent Teams for shared task lists and direct coordination; subagents for isolated parallel workers that report back. Only use multi-agent when phases are genuinely asynchronous or involve different specialists.

Playwright MCP is the community standard for AI-driven browser testing and visual verification. Pair with Claude in Chrome for day-to-day development; use Playwright MCP for pre-release test suite runs. Microsoft's Playwright CLI companion uses ~4x fewer tokens per session than streaming full accessibility trees.

LLM wiki / agent memory pattern (Karpathy): maintain a wiki/ of structured markdown that the agent reads and updates cross-session. raw/ holds immutable sources; wiki/ is LLM-maintained. Prevents context degradation across long projects.

Skills > one-shot prompts: package repeated task shapes as slash-command skills files in .claude/. Community-validated skills repos (gstack, mattpocock/sandcastle, hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code) provide reusable starting points.
Tool stacking is the norm: 70% of engineers use 2-4 AI coding tools simultaneously. Default pattern in 2026: Cursor for in-editor editing, Claude Code for complex multi-file tasks and agents.
